### God’s Instruction
Author: Thomas Brewer
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/gods-instruction
Passage: Psalm 25:12
Points:
- Unexpected trials and disruptions frequently make it hard to see where God is leading.
- Psalm 25:12 promises that the Lord will instruct those who fear Him in the path chosen.
- This instruction highlights both the believer's God-fearing choices and the Lord's sovereign guidance.
- God purposefully uses suffering and difficult seasons to instruct His children and lead them to joy.
- Trusting in the Lord's complete sovereignty brings true peace and quiet confidence.

### Intimacy Comes Through Trembling: The Surprising Path to More of God
Author: Jon Bloom
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/intimacy-comes-through-trembling
Passage: Psalm 25:14
Points:
- Experiencing God's grace always awakens a deeper hunger to know Him more intimately.
- Scripture reveals that the close friendship of the Lord belongs to those who fear Him.
- Authentic closeness with the Almighty involves reverent awe and holy trembling rather than casual familiarity.
- God loves His people too much to leave their sin unaddressed, often refining them through trials.
- Seeking greater intimacy requires embracing both God's tender mercy and His righteous severity.

### Forgiven for Jesus’s Sake
Author: John Piper
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/forgiven-for-jesuss-sake
Passage: Psalm 25:11
Points:
- God's righteousness is His supreme commitment to uphold and delight in His own glory.
- The psalmist appeals for the pardon of great iniquity based entirely on the Lord's name.
- Christ vindicated the Father's honor on the cross, making grace possible for sinners.
- Praying for forgiveness for God's name's sake is equivalent to praying in Jesus's name.
- Believers can seek forgiveness with confidence because Jesus paid the full debt for sin.

### How to Study in Vain: Why Every Subject Needs the Spirit
Author: Seth Porch
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/how-to-study-in-vain
Passage: Psalm 25:4–5
Points:
- Human minds remain limited and darkened without the illuminating work of the Holy Spirit.
- The prayer of Psalm 25:4–5 reflects a humble dependence on God to perceive divine truth.
- Every aspect of the created world was designed to direct our attention and praise to God.
- Pursuing learning purely through independent human reason results in futile vanity.
- The Spirit opens our eyes to recognize God's wisdom, beauty, and providence in all knowledge.
